## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:


```{r}
# REQUIRED PACKAGES

library(robCompositions)
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyquant)
library(quantmod)
library(readr)
library(here)
library(dplyr)
library(easyCODA)
library(factoextra)
library(cluster)
library(compositions)
library(ggplot2)
```


```{r}
# DATASET

bootstrap_2024_data <- read_csv(here("S&P500 2024 (work).csv"))
data_2024 <- as.data.frame(bootstrap_2024_data)

d_f <- read_csv(here("S&P500 2024 (work).csv"))
reduced_2024 <- as.data.frame(d_f)

reduced_2024 <- data.frame(
  Cyclical = d_f[,1] + d_f[,3] + d_f[,4] + d_f[6] + d_f[,10],
  Defensive = d_f[,2] + d_f[,7] + d_f[,9],
  Sensitive = d_f[,5] + d_f[,8] + d_f[,11],
  PriceChange = d_f[,12],
  Volatility = d_f[,13]
)

colnames(reduced_2024) <- c("Cyclical", "Defensive", "Sensitive", "PriceChange", "Volatility")
```

```{r}
data_2024 <- na.omit(data_2024)
```



```{r}
# MODEL FOR 2024 Price Change

X <- data_2024[,1:11]
X[X == 0] <- 0.1
Y <- data_2024[,12]

model_1 <- lmCoDaX(Y, X, method="classical")$ilr
model_1
```

```{r}
# USING lm FUNCTION

X <- data_2024[,1:11]
X[X == 0] <- 0.1
Y <- data_2024[,12]

model1 <- lm(Y ~ ilr(X))


a = coef(model1)[1]
print(a)

b = ilrInv(coef(model1)[-1],orig=X)
print(b)

varb=ilrvar2clr(vcov(model1)[-1,-1])
print(varb)
```

```{r}
set_par <- par(mar=c(3,3,0,0))
pred_values = predict(model1) 

plot(pred_values, Y)

abline(0,1)
par(set_par)
```

```{r}
cor(Y,pred_values,method="pearson")
```

```{r}
# Q-Q shows no significant deviation from normality - expected since data randomly generated
# Residuals are homoscedastic
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(model1,add.smooth=FALSE,which=1:2)
```

```{r}
studentresid = rstudent(model1)
qqnorm(StudentizedResiduals)
qqline(StudentizedResiduals)
shapiro.test(StudentizedResiduals)
boxplot(StudentizedResiduals)
```




```{r}
# MODEL FOR 2024 Volatility

X <- data_2024[,1:11]
X[X == 0] <- 0.1
Y <- data_2024[,13]

model_2 <- lmCoDaX(Y, X, method="classical")$ilr
model_2
```


```{r}
# USING lm FUNCTION

X <- data_2024[,1:11]
X[X == 0] <- 0.1
Y <- log(data_2024[,13])

model2 <- lm(Y ~ ilr(X))

a = coef(model2)[1]
print(a)

b = ilrInv(coef(model2)[-1],orig=X)
print(b)

varb=ilrvar2clr(vcov(model2)[-1,-1])
print(varb)
```

```{r}
set_par <- par(mar=c(3,3,0,0))
pred_values = predict(model2) 

plot(exp(pred_values), exp(Y))

abline(0,1)
par(set_par)
```

```{r}
cor(Y,Predicted,method="pearson")
```

```{r}
par(mfrow=c(2,2))
plot(model2,add.smooth=FALSE,which=1:2)
```
